clue.text: Iambic verse of song that's short and clear

indicators.note: Something cut short stops before its proper end, so the word named here gives up its final letter.

blocks.note: SONG docked of its last letter
what is left clear after every deduction is the net amount

explanation.surface: A song that is brief and easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' is the accountant's sense: the sum that survives all deductions is clear of them. 'Iambic' narrows the definition from any verse to a fixed fourteen-line form written in that metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, and in English it is written in iambic pentameter, so 'iambic verse' names its metre.

clue.text: Bejewelled ring is pale when lit by day

indicators.note: 'Lit' is slang for drunk rather than illuminated, and nothing a drunk is handed stays in the order it was given.

blocks.note: a ring is drawn as the letter O
the six letters of IS PALE, taken in another order
d = day

explanation.surface: A jewelled ring looking washed out in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit by day' is one phrase in the surface and two separate jobs beneath it: the drunkenness sits in 'lit', and the day hands over an abbreviation. The stone doing the bejewelling is named nowhere in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opalised has been turned to opal or set with the stone, so a ring treated that way is bejewelled.

clue.text: Jog naked, skirting centre of Tangier

indicators.note: To skirt a thing is to pass round its edge, so the word before it goes round what follows.
The centre of a word is the letter with equal numbers either side of it, and that letter alone is taken.

blocks.note: naked = nude
the middle letter of the seven in TANGIER

explanation.surface: Running round the middle of a Moroccan city with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' is the elbow in the ribs, not the trot round the park — the definition looks like part of the streaker's run. Tangier is the Moroccan port at the mouth of the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A jog of the elbow and a nudge are the same small prod, and both also mean prompting someone into action.

clue.text: Who ranted when performing type of play?

indicators.note: A performance turns what is written on the page into something else, so these letters may be taken in any arrangement.

blocks.note: the nine letters of WHO RANTED in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking which actor was the one shouting on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is earning its keep: the clue is a genuine question in the surface and a definition by example underneath. A two-hander is a piece written for exactly two actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-hander is a play with a cast of two, so it names one particular type of play rather than any drama.

clue.text: Comes up to ride with heroes on the wing

blocks.note: to ride a breaking wave is to surf
an ace is a fighter pilot credited with five or more kills

explanation.surface: Rising up to go riding with airborne heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes up' looks like the start of a sentence about approaching someone and is the definition, standing on its own. The heroes are in the air, so the ride beside them reads as flight rather than water.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to come up from below — a submarine, a diver, or a piece of news that finally reaches the light.

clue.text: Legume on base adapted over year

indicators.note: Anything adapted has been reshaped for a new use, so these letters may be taken in any order.
To lie over something is to cover it, so the reshaped letters close over the letter that comes next.

blocks.note: the six letters of ON BASE, taken in another order
y = year

explanation.surface: A crop at an army base bred to do better over a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word at the front, though 'Legume on base' reads as one phrase about something growing there. The base belongs entirely to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The soybean is a bean, and beans are legumes — seeds carried in a pod, the family that fixes nitrogen in the soil.

clue.text: Prepare component in urea dye

indicators.note: A component sits inside the thing it is part of, so the answer lies within the words that follow.

blocks.note: five consecutive letters running from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: One ingredient of a dye made from urea.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run straight across the gap between two words, which is where a concealed answer is hardest to see. 'Prepare' is the verb sense, making a thing fit for use.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready something is to prepare it, the verb built straight out of the adjective.

clue.text: Bold rogue returned with debts and after gold

indicators.note: To return is to come back the way you went, so those letters are read from the end to the start — up the column, in a down entry.
What comes after a thing is placed behind it, so the metal named last is set down first and everything else trails it.

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, from the Latin aurum
a cad is a rogue, his three letters coming back the other way
an IOU is a written debt, so several of them are IOUs

explanation.surface: A scoundrel coming home owing money, having gone off prospecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cad' is the crossword's standard rogue, a word that survives mainly in puzzles and old comic novels. The gold is the chemist's, taken from the periodic table rather than the jeweller's window.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone audacious takes risks a careful person would not, which is one shade of bold — daring, and often cheeky with it.

clue.text: Illegal drug at night gets daughter high

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, the crossword's standard illegal drug
something happening at night happens late
d = daughter

explanation.surface: Someone slipping their daughter something illegal after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, and its drug sense is exactly what the surface is offering you — the answer wants the mood instead. 'At night' asks for lateness, not an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be high is to be in soaring spirits, and elated is that lift — a sense with nothing to do with the clue's chemistry.

clue.text: Eisteddfod winner cried like lamb, we hear

indicators.note: 'We hear' says the answer arrives by ear, so it is the sound of the words that counts and not their spelling.

blocks.note: a lamb's cry is a baa, so a lamb that cried has baaed

explanation.surface: A festival prizewinner making a noise like a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: An eisteddfod is the Welsh festival of music and poetry, whose chief prize crowns a poet. The sound only lands in a British accent, where that R goes unpronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The bard is the poet crowned at a Welsh eisteddfod, the winner of its senior literary prize.

clue.text: May Nazi sod corrupt conceited king?

indicators.note: To corrupt a thing is to rot it out of its proper shape, so the letters before it no longer stand where they were put.

blocks.note: the ten letters of MAY NAZI SOD in a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some Nazi swine might lead a vain monarch astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes 'May' look like a politician's surname when it is only the ordinary verb opening a question. Ozymandias is Shelley's sonnet on a shattered desert statue, and the Greek name for Rameses II.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's Ozymandias is the 'king of kings' whose ruined statue still orders the mighty to look on his works and despair.

clue.text: Vibration from the East is current hail

indicators.note: Across the grid, whatever comes from the east is travelling westwards, so the word after it is written leftwards.

blocks.note: the two letters of IS, taken right to left
whatever is current is new
ave is the Latin for hail, as in Ave Maria

explanation.surface: A tremor out of the East, greeted as the latest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' sits next to a vibration and looks electrical; it wants the everyday sense instead. The hail at the end is the greeting, not the falling ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sine wave is the smooth up-and-down curve a vibrating string or a pure tone traces out over time.

clue.text: Eccentric, creaky person prone to gas

indicators.note: Something eccentric is off its proper centre, so these letters are not left sitting where they belong.

blocks.note: the six letters of CREAKY in a new order

explanation.surface: An odd, arthritic sort who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is the slang for idle talk rather than anything in a pipe, which is the step that makes the long definition readable. 'Eccentric' does double duty as a character note in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to talk on and on, and a yacker is someone who does exactly that — a nattering, never-quiet sort.

clue.text: Like chestnut-mounted thug in fairy tale

blocks.note: a chestnut horse is a reddish brown, so something like one is red
a rider mounted on a horse is riding
a hood is a hoodlum, an American gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster out riding a chestnut horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour, and the hyphen dresses the first two pieces up as one compound describing the thug. The wolf's victim gives her name to the whole story.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Riding Hood is the tale of the girl in the red cloak and the wolf at grandmother's, printed under that title with or without its 'Little'.

clue.text: Concerning papers editor controlled

blocks.note: re = concerning, the heading on a memo
the press is the newspapers taken together
ed = editor

explanation.surface: About the newspapers a certain editor kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Three journalism words in a row, each one a staple abbreviation or synonym, which is what lets the clue read as a single sentence about Fleet Street. The definition is the last word and belongs to psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a feeling is to hold it down and keep it out of sight, which is controlling it rather than letting it show.

clue.text: Sincere to try and quit, regressing tons

indicators.note: To regress is to travel back the way you came, so the word before it is read from its end — upwards, in a down entry.

blocks.note: a court tries a case by hearing it
someone who quit a place left it, and those letters come back the other way
t = tons

explanation.surface: An honest attempt to give up, with the tonnage sliding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the courtroom's, where a judge tries a case by hearing it — the sense a solver reaches for last after 'to try and quit' has read as one plain phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartfelt apology comes from the heart rather than from manners, so it is sincere — genuinely and deeply meant.

clue.text: Defeat inspiring anger with defence

indicators.note: To inspire is literally to breathe in, so the word doing the breathing draws what follows inside itself.

blocks.note: the fall of a city is its defeat
ire is anger
w = with

explanation.surface: A rout that rouses fury in the people defending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' is the breathing-in sense, not the uplifting one, and it is the only word saying that anything goes inside. The little word 'with' is a letter rather than joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A firewall is the blank wall built to stop flames spreading between buildings, and the computing sense keeps intruders out the same way.

clue.text: Fair play when Spanish drunk drinks fortified wines at Mass

indicators.note: Someone drunk is in no state to keep anything in order, so the letters before it may be taken in any arrangement.
To drink a thing down is to take it inside you, so what follows lands within the letters already shuffled.

blocks.note: the seven letters of SPANISH, taken in another order
port is a wine fortified with brandy
m = mass

explanation.surface: A drunken Spaniard knocking back the port during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M is physics' mass dressed up as the Catholic service, which is also what lets the fortified wines stand beside it without looking out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmanship is playing by the rules and treating an opponent decently, which is fair play in the language of the field.

clue.text: Vacated street with loads of paper runs

indicators.note: A vacated building has had everybody out of the middle of it, so the word keeps only the letters at either end.

blocks.note: STREET emptied of everything between its first and last letters
a ream is five hundred sheets, so reams are loads of paper

explanation.surface: An empty street knee-deep in paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacated' is an instruction to empty a word out rather than a description of the street. The definition is the last word, and it is what water does, not what a person does.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that streams runs in a steady flow, so the two verbs describe the same movement down a channel or a hillside.

clue.text: As charity, give fellow crown, not pence

indicators.note: 'Not' rules the coin that follows out of the reckoning, so its letter is taken away from what came before.

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
the crown of the head is the pate, here short of a letter
p = pence, and this is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Handing a college fellow a coin, but keeping back the small change.
explanation.walkthrough: The crown is the top of the head, not the old five-shilling piece — and 'pence' is sitting right beside it to keep you thinking about coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to hand something over to a good cause; the giving is ordinary, and the charitable destination is what the word adds.

clue.text: Discovered phoney saint is lacking guile

indicators.note: Read as dis-covered, the word has had its covering removed, so the letters capping each end come off.

blocks.note: PHONEY stripped of the letter at either end
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A bogus saint exposed at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' means found out in the surface, where a fraud is being unmasked, and comes apart into dis-covered in the wordplay. The saint arrives as the usual two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honest has no tricks in them and nothing concealed, which is what lacking guile describes.

clue.text: Variety of steak is black in hue

indicators.note: What is in something sits within it, so the letter named goes inside the word that follows.

blocks.note: a tone is a shade or hue of a colour
b = black, the grade stamped on a soft pencil

explanation.surface: A cut of meat burnt black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black in hue' reads as one description of the charred meat and is really two instructions with the insertion between them. The enumeration promises a single letter standing alone at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is the loin steak cut across the bone, and the bone's shape in the middle of it is what gives the cut its name.

clue.text: Trainee misplaced the last of finder's fee

indicators.note: Something misplaced is no longer where it was put, so these letters are free to settle anywhere.
The last of a word is its closing letter, and that single letter is all that is taken.

blocks.note: seven letters waiting to be shuffled, with one more to join them
the closing letter of FINDER, the possessive 's belonging to the surface alone

explanation.surface: A raw recruit mislaying the reward paid for finding something.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'finder's fee' down the middle: half of it supplies a letter and half is the definition. The fee meant is the one that keeps a professional on call, not a payment per job.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is the sum paid to keep a lawyer or agent available, a fee for holding a claim on their time.

clue.text: Peruvian with fashion-forward loo

indicators.note: Forward is towards the front, so the piece it is attached to leads and the rest comes behind.

blocks.note: whatever is in fashion is simply in
the can is American slang for the lavatory

explanation.surface: A Peruvian whose lavatory is the last word in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion-forward' is one modish compound in the surface and comes apart into two instructions underneath. The definition is an adjective, describing something of the empire rather than naming a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes anything belonging to the Inca, whose empire was centred on Cuzco in what is now Peru.

clue.text: Enthused to stick around, she's first on isle

indicators.note: Going around something means closing about it, so the word before opens up and takes the rest inside.
Being first means both the opening letter of the word before it and the place that letter then takes.

blocks.note: paste is what you stick things down with
the opening letter of SHE
Iona is a tiny island off the west coast of Scotland, famous for its abbey

explanation.surface: A keen girl hanging about, the first to reach the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' is one idiom in the surface and two separate instructions beneath it. Iona is where Columba founded his monastery, and setters keep it handy for its four obliging letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionate is fired up about what they are doing, which is exactly what being enthused describes.

clue.text: Say rocker's dropping recipe for tea

indicators.note: To drop a thing is to let it fall away, so the letter named goes and the rest closes up.

blocks.note: a rocker is, for example, the seat that sits on curved runners
R heads a prescription, from the Latin recipe, 'take'

explanation.surface: A rock musician who has mislaid his recipe for a brew.
explanation.walkthrough: The rocker is furniture rather than a leather-jacketed musician, and 'say' is what quietly signals the example. The R comes off a doctor's prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is tea — the word for it across South Asia and much of the world, and the spiced milky version on British menus.

clue.text: Uncalled-for heckles ending in distress

indicators.note: A word's ending is its final letter, so only the last letter of what follows is wanted.

blocks.note: to needle someone is to heckle or provoke them
the final letter of DISTRESS

explanation.surface: Jeering that finishes with somebody upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heckles' is a verb here, not the neck feathers of a cockerel, and it has to stay in the third person for the letters to work. The definition is the hyphenated phrase at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A needless remark was never required — uncalled-for in the sense of unnecessary, which is also how an unkind one gets described.

clue.text: Initial slice of tuna fish in mess

indicators.note: An initial slice is the first cut taken off the front, so only the opening letter of the word comes away.

blocks.note: the opening letter of TUNA
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: The first slice off a tuna, served in the officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The mess of the surface is the hall where servicemen eat, and the definition wants a muddle instead. 'Fish' is the verb, which is the harder half to spot when a tuna has just been named.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a snarled knot of string or hair, and any mess of that twisted-together sort.
